2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, intended to acquire about 907 Bigha 09 biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".

The LAC (N/W) after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 907 bighas 09 biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests besides liquidated cost for trees, tubewell and borings.

4. It is stated that the petitioners are the cobhumidhar in land bearing khasra no. 39/4 (416),

sentences.text: 5. It is stated that the compensation awarded by the learned LAC is too low, unjust, arbitrary without any reasonable basis and the same is not acceptable to the petitioners.
The petitioners are recorded bhumidhars of the said land which has been acquired vide the said order.
The said land is very fertile and also gives handsome income to the petitioners in the form of 34 crops in a year.

6. It is stated that the said land is situated in village Rani Khera and is well connected with roads from all sides at the time of acquisition and was having great potential value for the residential as well as commercial purposes.
The said land is duly levelled and as such gives handsome income to the petitioners.
7. It is stated that the said land is situated near NH10, Rohtak Road, Delhi and is having a great potential value as a perfect building/commercial site.

The building activities and commercial activities is coming up for last more than 15 years and, therefore, the said land has great potential value and the market value of the said land is more than Rs. 10,000 per square yards

. It is stated that all kind of civic amenities i.e. electricity, water, road, bus service, telephone, school, college were situated in and around the said land and the said land has great potential value.

There are many residential colonies in and around the said land, which shows the great potential value of said land at the time of passing of the notification under Section 4 of the Act and as such the said land could easily get Rs. 10,000 per square yards.

The notices under Section 9 and 10 were issued to the landowners/interested persons inviting claims/objections of the said land.

Pursuant to the notices, claims were filed by the affected persons claiming different value of their land and,
thereafter, the said award has been passed.

13. It is admitted that the claim of the petitioners with respect to measurements apportionment and compensation of the said land is admitted to the extent of the said award and the learned LAC has assessed the value of the said land in respect of the correct market value prevailing at the time of the notification.

Various factors were taken into account by the learned LAC while assessing the market value of the said land and, now the petitioners are claiming excessive and exorbitant enhancement of the said land and structures.
The Delhi Land Reforms Act is applicable to the said land and the petitioners are not entitled for compensation in respect of any construction or structure which is raised without sanctioning of law.

sentences.text: I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.
My issue wise findings and determination are as under:  WHETHER THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED TO ENHANCEMENT IN COMPENSATION, IF SO, TO WHAT AMOUNT ? OPP 24.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioners.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the said land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioners.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
25.

27. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Rani Khera are covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court in the case of Muktyari Singh Vs. UOI (supra),
this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

28. In the Mukhtyar Singh (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/ per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre has been given.

RELIEF 30.

In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs:
(i) Fair Market value of land of petitioner as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,73,583/ per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre is accordingly accorded.

(ii) Additional amount @ 12% (in terms of Section 23(1A) of the Act).

(iv) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
31.
Reference petition is accordingly answered with direction to parties to bear their own respective costs.

rpc_texts: The petitioners are accordingly entitled to the same compensation for his land as was awarded in Ram Kishan (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,73,583/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre.
The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.

In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs:
(i) Fair Market value of land of petitioner as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,73,583/ per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre is accordingly accorded.

(ii) Additional amount @ 12% (in terms of Section 23(1A) of the Act).
(iii) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation ( in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(iv) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
31.
Reference petition is accordingly answered with direction to parties to bear their own respective costs.
